samples: This module filters a list of tasks to those due within a chosen number of days from today, sorted earliest first, and counts the Monday-to-Friday days left until each one (not counting today, counting the due day, and ignoring public holidays). It also includes a reader that turns lines like "title, date" into tasks and reports a missing comma or an invalid date. However, the runnable `main` only uses three hardcoded sample tasks with fixed 2026 dates and prints those due within ten days, so it is a demo rather than a finished tool, and the line reader is never used by it. The filtering and counting functions are reusable, but you would need to write your own entry point to feed them real data.

This module offers small date helpers: reading a "title, date" line into a task, counting Monday-to-Friday days after a start date up to and including an end date, and listing tasks due within a given number of days, earliest first. It does not read real input, though. Its entry point checks three hardcoded sample tasks with fixed autumn-2026 due dates against the current date, so it prints nothing unless it runs within ten days of one of them. Weekends are the only days excluded (holidays are ignored), so reuse the helper functions rather than the program itself, and only if that simple calendar rule is enough for you.

This module provides reusable pieces for deadline tracking: reading a "title, date" line into a task (reporting a missing comma or a bad date as failures), counting the Monday-to-Friday days after one date up to and including another, and selecting the tasks due within a given number of days, earliest first. Its runnable `main` is only a demo: it takes three hard-coded tasks with dates in late 2026, compares them against the real current date, and prints each one due in the next ten days along with its working days left. The line parser is never used by `main`, and working days ignore public holidays, so use it as a small library to build on rather than a finished tool, and expect the demo to print nothing if today's date is far from those sample dates.

This program picks out tasks due within a number of days from today, sorted earliest first, and for each one reports how many Monday-to-Friday days remain, counting after today up to and including the due date. It also has a helper that reads a "title, date" line into a task and reports a missing comma or an invalid date as errors. However, the runnable entry point uses three hardcoded sample tasks dated in late 2026 and a ten-day window from the current date, so it prints only the samples that fall in that window, which may be none. It never uses the line parser, and it ignores holidays, so treat it as a reusable date-and-deadline toolkit rather than a finished task tracker.

This module defines a task with a due date, a reader that turns a line of "title, date" text into a task (reporting a missing comma or an invalid date), a counter of Monday-to-Friday days between two dates, and a filter that returns the tasks due within a given number of days, earliest first. Its runnable entry point is only a demo: it takes three hard-coded sample tasks with dates in October and November 2026, uses today's date, and prints each task due in the next ten days with its working days left, so the output depends on when you run it and may be empty. The line reader is not used by that entry point, and the working-day count ignores public holidays, so it is useful as a small library of date helpers but not yet as a finished tool for your own task list.
